docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The block diagram shows the initial subsection of the drowsy driver device. This subsystem reads the light values of the surrounding area and will send an analog signal to the next subsystem to to start the next sensor. The system runs on 5V power, ran through a fuse to ensure power surges don't ruin the components. The fuse is connected to an op amp attached to the photoresistor. The system also includes a button and LED for debugging purposes.

docs.title: Photoresistor
docs.text:
Component Image Pros Cons GL5528 * Verified to work * Average values for maximum voltage and gamma value * Least detailed datasheet * Lowest spectral response peak (540nm) NSL-06-062(S) * Highest gamma value at 10-100lux (0.8) * Highest spectral response peak (550nm) * Not epoxy coated * Lowest maximum voltage (100V) GL205 * Highest maximum voltage (500V) * Most extensive datasheet * Lowest gamma value at 10-100lux (0.6) * Only orderable in bulk

Decision: GL5528 Photoresistor

Rationale: This photoresistor is the most commonly used model in Arduino kits because its values are average across the board. While it doesn't have the highest maximum voltage, the design of the subsystem won't need it to exceed 100V. The higher gamma value of NSL-06-062 be a benefit, but the higher sensitivity could lead to issues with detecting the street lights at night.

docs.title: Op Amp
docs.text:
Component Image Pros Cons LM741 * Highest maximum voltage (22V) * High supply current (1.7mA) * Least amount of pins * Slow speed (0.3μs) OPA4131 * Most amount of pins (tied) * High bandwidth (4MHz) * Unknown supply current rating MCP6004 * Most amount of pins (tied) * Rail to rail capability * Very low power drain (100μA) * Lowest maximum voltage (7V) * Low speed (0.6μs)

Decision: MCP6004 Op Amp

Rationale: This Op Amp is the most powerful of the three with the rail-to-rail capabilities and low power drain. It has enough pins to work for the subsystem without adding extra pins like the OPA4131. Can operate on voltages as low as 1.8V, which is within the calculated range for this subsystem.

docs.title: 5V Power Supply
docs.text:
Component Image Pros Cons E36155A * Highest power capabilities (60V) * Big and clunky * Must be plugged in U280-C02-63W-1B * Uses power from car * Built-in overload protection * Wires can get in the way * Requires external wires to use TPS61023 * Most portable option * Attached to subsystem * Smallest option * Requires small battery * Variable max output

Decision: TPS61023

Rationale: This is the smallest and lightest option that doesn't require the user to need wires. It can be used with a removeable battery for easy switching for the driver. It's also the most portable option, allowing the user to use the device outside of their car, if necessary.
